name: grain-crest
title: Grain Crest
description: Sortable data-table column headers where each one carries a one-line braille micro-histogram of its own column's distribution, so skew, outliers and bimodality are answered before anyone sorts.
useWhen: data-table column headers where the sort control and 'what does this column look like' question are the same 16-glyph strip — numeric columns get a log-aware braille histogram (skewed columns get a small ᴸ tag), categorical columns get a dominance bar for the top category's share, and a ▸ marker eases along the strip on sort to show where the row now on top sits in that distribution. Pick sparkline-ascii or stat-row-baseline-spark instead when the shape to show is a trend over time on a row or stat tile — most table columns have no time axis, so a trendline there would misrepresent the data; grain-crest never plots time, only static distribution shape.
instruction: Sortable <table> column headers that each stack three lines inside their sort button: (1) the label, an optional small aria-hidden ᴸ tag, and a caret that fills in and rotates on the active column; (2) a 16-glyph aria-hidden strip computed from that column's own values — numeric columns render a histogram on the braille fill ramp ' ⣀⣤⣶⣿' (0..4 dots-per-cell, bottom-anchored), log-binned (edges = min·(max/min)^(i/16)) with the ᴸ tag shown whenever max/median >= 4 so a right-skewed column doesn't collapse into one saturated bin; categorical columns render a dominance bar instead — filled cells (⣿, text-foreground) sized to round(topShare*16), remainder as a dim track (⣀, text-ns-muted/40); (3) a fixed-height marker track. RENDERING: plain semantic <table> in a rounded-md border border-border bg-background card — no canvas, no SVG chart, DOM+CSS only (one 8x8 inline <svg> per header is just the sort caret icon). INTERACTION: clicking a header's button (type=button, native Enter/Space) sorts the whole table by that column, numeric defaulting to descending and categorical to ascending on first click, toggling direction on repeat clicks of the same column; the crest itself never changes shape, since sorting doesn't change the data — instead, on the active column only, a ▸ marker (text-ns-accent, position:absolute, left set inline and eased with transition: left 550ms cubic-bezier(0.19,1,0.22,1), disabled to an instant snap when prefers-reduced-motion) shows where the row now on top of the table sits inside that column's OWN distribution: for numeric columns, the bin its value falls into; for categorical, the middle of the dominant zone if the top row's category is the dominant one, otherwise the middle of the non-dominant remainder. Toggling direction on the same column flips which end the top row's value sits near, which is what actually drives the marker's slide. Hovering a strip (onPointerMove computing a bin/segment from cursor fraction) writes a plain-text line — bin range and row count, or category and share — into a shared detail bar below the table (not a floating tooltip); focusing a header button writes that column's full stat summary into the same bar as a sighted keyboard-parity affordance, cleared on blur/pointerleave. TOKENS: --foreground, --ns-muted (including a /40 opacity cut for the dominance track), --border, --background, --ns-accent reserved for the marker and the focus ring — never for the histogram or dominance-bar ink itself, so accent stays interaction-only. A11Y: standard th[aria-sort=ascending|descending] (omitted, not 'none', when the column isn't the active sort — matches the rest of the registry), the header's real accessible name is a computed aria-label of the form '<Label>, sortable, median 120ms, range 40 to 2100, right-skewed' (or 'sorted ascending'/'descending' once active, and a categorical form giving category count and top share) so the crest's information survives without vision even though the glyphs themselves are aria-hidden; Tab reaches every header button in DOM order, resting state has no marker in the DOM at all (mounts only once a column is sorted). DEMO: a 16-row 'request latency by route' table — Latency (ms, right-skewed 42..2100, gets the ᴸ tag), Cost ($, roughly linear, no tag), Region and Status (categorical dominance bars) — plus a leading, non-sortable Endpoint identity column so the table's first interactive control is unambiguously a grain header.
